_comment: Scale-gate thresholds for tools/bot_swarm/scale_gate.py (issue #520). Single source of truth for the gate numbers. See docs/developer/load-testing.md. Transport policy (#773): GameNetworkingSockets is the DEFAULT internet transport (#507), so every headline/characterisation profile pins `transport: gns` — the published numbers describe what ships. enet6 (the LAN/single-player backend) keeps two regression legs: `pr` (every PR, hosted runner) and `reference-enet` (128-client strict tier).

pr._comment: Deterministic PR tier: only machine-independent metrics are hard-gated (bandwidth + admission + KB/s baseline). tick-Hz is a total-collapse tripwire; tick-ms is advisory (0 = disabled) because the client-side proxy and CPU timing are noisy on shared runners. Deliberately enet6 (bot_swarm's default): it is the enet6 regression instrument, and an enet6-only build keeps the PR leg lean (no protobuf/OpenSSL). SENSOR-LOADED since #1089: bots fly builtin:sensor-fighter against ai_entity_count hostiles, so ContactTables populate and datalink team fusion actually runs. Before that every table was empty, fusion merged nothing, and the headline numbers described a hollow battlespace -- the two systems most likely to break at 128 players were the two this gate could not see.

reference._comment: The PRIMARY reference profile (#773): 128 clients with BOTH ends on GNS (FL_LOADTEST_TRANSPORT=gns -> fl-server --transport gns + bot_swarm --transport gns) — the default internet transport is the one the headline numbers describe. Strict tick-ms p99 on the 8-core/16GB reference instance (or a self-hosted runner via --strict); advisory on hosted runners. REQUIRES an FL_ENABLE_GNS=ON build: bot_swarm hard-fails rather than silently falling back to enet6, and the gate cross-checks the report's `transport` key, so a downgraded run fails instead of passing as a GNS validation. Baselined per-profile; the wire KB/s baseline is the one that tracks what the transport actually costs (#772 — enet6 range-coder-compresses, GNS encrypts and does not compress). SENSOR-LOADED since #1089: bots fly builtin:sensor-fighter against ai_entity_count hostiles, so ContactTables populate and datalink team fusion actually runs. Before that every table was empty, fusion merged nothing, and the headline numbers described a hollow battlespace -- the two systems most likely to break at 128 players were the two this gate could not see.

reference-enet._comment: enet6 regression leg at full reference scale (#773; this was the pre-#773 `reference` profile). enet6 is the LAN/single-player backend and a genuine regression instrument (net_check, bot_swarm's default), so it keeps a 128-client strict-tier gate — but its figures are NOT the headline capacity numbers; those come from `reference` (GNS, what ships). SENSOR-LOADED since #1089: bots fly builtin:sensor-fighter against ai_entity_count hostiles, so ContactTables populate and datalink team fusion actually runs. Before that every table was empty, fusion merged nothing, and the headline numbers described a hollow battlespace -- the two systems most likely to break at 128 players were the two this gate could not see.

soak._comment: 2 h soak-stability run on the shipping transport (GNS, #773). Same strict thresholds as `reference`; the server self-reports RSS in the tick metrics (#707). The leak gate hard-fails if endpoint growth exceeds assert_max_rss_growth_kb (~256 MiB over 2 h) OR if the RSS growth TREND fitted over the run's tail exceeds assert_max_rss_slope_kb_per_min (#789) — the trend catches a slow leak that stayed under the endpoint bound. bot_swarm samples RSS every 30 s (240 points over 2 h) and fits the final half. SENSOR-LOADED since #1089: bots fly builtin:sensor-fighter against ai_entity_count hostiles, so ContactTables populate and datalink team fusion actually runs. Before that every table was empty, fusion merged nothing, and the headline numbers described a hollow battlespace -- the two systems most likely to break at 128 players were the two this gate could not see.

entity-scale._comment: Entity-pool + SpatialIndex scaling characterisation (#573), re-derived on GNS (#773). Sweeps entity count x sim worker count via FL_TEST_SPAWN_AI / FL_SIM_WORKER_THREADS, driven from the [world] load-spawn affordance. Advisory only (baselined=false): reads server_tick.entities + tick p99 into the summary but never gates the committed KB/s baseline. assert_max_tick_ms is DELIBERATELY 0 (#773): the reference-runner workflow leg always passes --strict, which would turn a tick-ms threshold into a hard bot_swarm assert and fail the sweep's deliberately-collapsing single-worker cells — which ARE the characterisation, not a regression (the advisory summary still records per-cell tick p99). Reference-tier (workflow_dispatch) — needs the 8-core reference box for meaningful CPU timing.

overrun._comment: Synthetic tick-overrun profile (#574): proves the #514 graceful overrun governor ENGAGES and SHEDS rather than spiralling — on GNS, the shipping transport (#773). Runs with the governor ON (governor=true -> FL_LOADTEST_GOVERNOR=1) and deterministically overloads a serialize-bound tick with test_spawn_ai=5000 at sim_workers=1. The 5000-entity overload carries over from enet6 UNCHANGED: at high entity counts the serialize cost is the engine's own per-peer encode/schedule work (entities x peers), not ENet's inline send — the #773 governor-off probe on the 8-core reference box measured ~24.6 Hz / 34.8 ms tick (serialize 32.5 ms, 93%) on GNS, an even larger collapse margin below 60 Hz than enet6's ~36.8 Hz (#573). Gates: max_load_factor 0.99 fails if the governor never engaged (load_factor stayed 1.0); max_dropped_ticks 100 is the graceful-not-spiral bound (a small allowance absorbs the one-time startup-spawn + EWMA-ramp transient; a genuine governor-off spiral measured ~1060 drops in just 30 s at this load); --assert-min-entities 5000 (auto from the load-spawn) confirms the overload took. baselined=false: the shed KB/s must NEVER touch the committed bandwidth baseline. Reference tier only (workflow_dispatch) — the collapse margin is reliable only on a controlled runtime.

congestion._comment: Synthetic congestion profile (#714): proves the #518 per-peer AIMD send-rate controller ENGAGES on a degraded link and RECOVERS when it clears — on GNS, the shipping transport (#773; GNS supplies real link stats via SteamNetConnectionRealTimeStatus_t ping/quality, so the controller's RTT-over-baseline trigger sees the degraded window the same way it does ENet's roundTripTime). bot_swarm routes its clients through a local lossy UDP proxy (transport-agnostic — it forwards datagrams) that drops 5% of datagrams + adds 100 ms one-way delay in a mid-run window ([25s, 55s) from proxy start — after the connect ramp, ending ~35s before the run ends so the additive ramp-up has a clean tail to recover in). The +100 ms delay (+200 ms RTT, far over the controller's 40 ms margin) is the deterministic engage trigger; the 5% loss is a secondary delivery stressor kept below the level that trips the transport's own peer timeout. Gates (schema v5 run-long watermarks): congestion_min_send_hz must fall to <= 30 (engaged; the controller floor is 10 Hz) and congestion_recovered_send_hz must climb back to >= 55 (recovered). baselined=false: degraded KB/s must never touch the committed bandwidth baseline. Reference tier only (workflow_dispatch).

weapons._comment: Weapons-at-scale characterisation (#583): 128 clients flying the `weapons` pattern (duty-cycled gun fire + staggered store releases), so the fire path, hitscan, projectile pool and the SnapshotEffects TLV all run under the reference load. On GNS, the shipping transport. This is the 'projectiles within budget at 128 clients' acceptance instrument: it hard-gates the collapse tripwires (tick-Hz floor + wire KB/s ceiling) but is baselined=false — projectile traffic is bursty and store-dependent, so its KB/s must NEVER touch the committed bandwidth baseline. tick-ms is advisory (0): the extra serialize load from projectile entities + effects TLV is the characterisation, not a regression. Reference tier (workflow_dispatch / nightly), like the other 128-client legs.

entity-churn._comment: Heavier-AI-mix + projectile-churn characterisation (#580, extends the #573 entity-scale matrix which deliberately used cheap static loiterers), re-derived on GNS (#773). Pre-spawns entities with a representative controller mix (60% loiter / 25% pursuit [EntityManager::get on a moving target each tick] / 15% patrol [a StateMachineController whose AnyEntityWithinRange transitions run SpatialIndex::queryRadius EVERY tick — the expensive AI path the governor's AI stride decimates]) and runs the projectile-churn generator (120 spawn+reap/s, 3 s TTL => ~360 extra live entities at steady state; continuous EntityPool alloc/free + SnapshotDespawn TLV traffic). Compare ai_ms / collision_ms / maintenance_ms against the same entity_spawn_counts points in the entity-scale matrix (docs/developer/decisions/entity-scale-characterization.md). Advisory only (baselined=false); assert_max_tick_ms deliberately 0, same reason as entity-scale (#773 — the collapsing cells are the data). Reference tier (workflow_dispatch on demand, like entity-scale).
